# QuickService.ts

<!-- Generated by `bun run agents:generate` from packages/cli/agent-docs/. Do not edit by hand. -->

QuickService.ts builds REST services on Bun from TypeScript types: entities in `entities/` become routes, validation, migrations and OpenAPI docs.

Workflow: `bunx quickservicets init <name> --db <database>` creates a project, you add entity types to `entities/`, `bun run build` (or `bun run dev`) generates `.generated/`, `bun run quickservicets migration add <Name>` and `bun run quickservicets migrate` create and apply the migrations, and the service answers on port 3000.

The agent guide topics are in `packages/cli/agent-docs/`: `overview`, `quickstart`, `entities`, `endpoints-and-hooks`, `config-and-env`, `features`, `testing`, `deploy`, `troubleshooting`. The docs site serves them with every page as Markdown from [/llms.txt](/llms.txt).

## Using QuickService.ts in a project

What QuickService.ts is, when to choose it for a backend and when to pick something else.

QuickService.ts builds REST services on Bun from TypeScript types. You write each entity as a `type` in `entities/`, and `quickservicets build` generates its CRUD routes, validation, filters, relations, file uploads, migrations, typed repositories and an OpenAPI document. Custom routes are files in `endpoints/`, shared request logic is hooks in `hooks/` attached with JSDoc tags, and scheduled work is jobs in `jobs/`. The same project runs on an in-memory database, SQLite, PostgreSQL or MongoDB.

The framework ships as three npm packages: `@quickservicets/core` (the runtime), `@quickservicets/cli` (the `quickservicets` command) and `quickservicets` (so `bunx quickservicets` runs that command without installing anything).

### Use it when

- The service is mostly records with rules: users, orders, projects, bookings, back offices, internal APIs.
- You want CRUD, validation, paging, filtering, sorting, relations and API docs without writing them.
- The team writes TypeScript and runs (or can run) Bun 1.4.2 or later.
- You need the database to be swappable: memory for tests, SQLite for small deployments, PostgreSQL or MongoDB in production.
- You want built-in features (rate limits, CORS, queues, write events, history, idempotency keys, ETags, feature flags, health routes) switched on with one config key.

### Do not use it when

- The runtime must be Node.js, Deno or a browser: the CLI and the server need Bun.
- The API is GraphQL or gRPC only, or mostly streaming media.
- The data model is not records: a pure proxy, a static site or a compute-only function.
- You must control every SQL statement of every route; QuickService.ts generates the data access and the migrations.

### How a project works

1. `bunx quickservicets init <name> --db <database>` creates the project in any folder.
2. You add entity types to `entities/`, endpoint files to `endpoints/`, hooks to `hooks/` and jobs to `jobs/`.
3. `bun run build` (or `bun run dev`, which also serves and rebuilds on save) writes `.generated/`: models, routes, types, the OpenAPI document and the server entry.
4. For SQLite, PostgreSQL and MongoDB, `quickservicets migration add <Name>` writes a migration from the model changes and `quickservicets migrate` applies it.
5. `bun run start` runs the last build in production.

Each entity `Task` in `entities/Task.ts` is served at `/tasks` (list, read, create, update, replace, delete) and is `repos.tasks` in endpoints, hooks and jobs.

Every topic ships with the CLI: `bunx quickservicets docs` lists them, `bunx quickservicets docs <topic>` prints one offline, and `bunx quickservicets docs search <term>` searches them with the CLI, config and tags reference.

Full docs: [Introduction](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/index.md)

### Do not

- Do not pick QuickService.ts for a Node.js-only runtime; it needs Bun.
- Do not hand-write CRUD routes for an entity; the build generates them.
- Do not edit files in `.generated/`; every build overwrites them.
- Do not write SQL migrations by hand; `quickservicets migration add <Name>` writes them from the model.
- Do not add Express, Hono or another HTTP framework; routes are files in `endpoints/`.

### Quickstart

The exact commands to go from an empty folder to a running QuickService.ts service with one entity on SQLite.

You need Bun 1.4.2 or later (`bun --version`). Run every step in order; each command is meant to be copied as it is.

#### 1. Create the project

In any folder outside another QuickService.ts project:

```bash
bunx quickservicets init my-api --db sqlite
cd my-api
bun install
```

`--db` takes `memory`, `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mongodb`. Always pass it: without it, `init` asks. SQLite needs nothing else installed and keeps its data in `data.db`; `memory` needs no migrations but loses its data on every restart. For `postgres` and `mongodb`, put the real connection settings in `.env` before step 4.

#### 2. Add an entity

Create `entities/Task.ts`. The file name and the exported type name must match, in PascalCase:

```ts
// entities/Task.ts
export type Task = {
  /** @minLength 1 */
  title: string;
  /** @default false */
  done: boolean;
  dueAt?: Date;
};
```

Never declare `id`, `createdAt` or `updatedAt`; every entity gets them.

#### 3. Build

```bash
bun run build
```

It prints `Built 3 entities, 0 custom endpoints and 0 hooks.` (the count includes the built-in `File` and `Media` entities) and writes `.generated/`.

#### 4. Create and apply the migration

SQLite, PostgreSQL and MongoDB need a migration for every model change (skip this step with `--db memory`):

```bash
bun run quickservicets migration add CreateTasks
bun run quickservicets migrate
```

`migration add` writes `migrations/<timestamp>_CreateTasks.ts` from the model; `migrate` applies it.

#### 5. Run the service

```bash
bun run dev
```

It prints `QuickService.ts listening on http://localhost:3000` and keeps running: it rebuilds and restarts on every saved change. Set `PORT=4000` before the command for another port. In a script, run it in the background and wait for that line.

#### 6. Call the API

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:3000/tasks -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"title":"Write the docs"}'
curl localhost:3000/tasks
```

The list answers `{"data":[...],"total":1,"limit":20,"offset":0}`. Filters use brackets, so pass `-g` to curl:

```bash
curl -g "localhost:3000/tasks?where[done][eq]=false&sort=-createdAt"
```

The API docs are at `http://localhost:3000/docs`.

#### After every model change

1. Edit or add files in `entities/`.
2. `bun run build` (`bun run dev` rebuilds by itself).
3. `bun run quickservicets migration add <Name>` with a name for the change, like `AddPriorityToTasks`.
4. `bun run quickservicets migrate`.

Run `bun run typecheck` after `bun run build` to type-check the project.

#### In scripts and agents

- Add `--json` to the commands that report results (`build`, `migration add`, `migration list`, `migrate`, `job list`, `job runs`, `env check`, and list commands like `queue list`): they print one JSON document to stdout, `{"ok":true,...}` or `{"ok":false,"error":{"code","message"}}`, and the logs to stderr.
- Add `--yes` (or run with `CI=true`) so no command ever waits for an answer: a question with a safe answer takes it, and one without exits 2 naming the flag to pass.
- Check the exit code: 0 success, 1 the operation failed, 2 usage error or a missing answer, 3 configuration error, 4 database unreachable.

```bash
bun run quickservicets migration list --json
bun run quickservicets migrate --json --yes
```

Full docs: [Getting started](docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/installation.md)

#### Do not

- Do not leave out `--db`; `init` would wait for an answer.
- Do not run `init` in a folder that has files; it stops with `Directory is not empty`.
- Do not skip `bun install`; the project depends on `@quickservicets/core` and `@quickservicets/cli`.
- Do not write migration files or SQL by hand, and do not edit an applied migration.
- Do not edit `.generated/`; rebuild instead.
- Do not start the service before `migrate` on SQLite, PostgreSQL or MongoDB; the tables would not exist.
- Do not use `npx`; use `bunx` and `bun run`.

## Working on this repository

- Bun workspaces: `packages/core` (`@quickservicets/core`), `packages/cli` (`@quickservicets/cli`), `packages/quickservicets` (the `bunx quickservicets` package), `docs` (the docs site), `benchmarks/quickservicets` and the projects in `examples/` and `examples/minimal/`. Run `bun install` once at the root.
- `bun test` at the root runs every test, `bun run typecheck` included. The PostgreSQL and MongoDB tests run only when `TEST_POSTGRES_URL` and `TEST_MONGODB_URL` are set (MongoDB as a replica set), like `TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgres://postgres:pass@localhost:5432/postgres TEST_MONGODB_URL='mongodb://localhost:27017/?replicaSet=rs0' bun test`; otherwise they are skipped.
- `bun run docs:reference` regenerates the reference pages after changing tags, config keys, CLI commands or documented error messages; a test fails while they are stale.
- `bun run agents:generate` regenerates this file, the skill in `skills/quickservicets/`, the plugin manifests in `.claude-plugin/` and the docs pages the CLI bundles in `packages/cli/docs-pages/` from the topics in `packages/cli/agent-docs/` and the docs pages; `bun run docs:reference` runs it too, and a test fails while they are stale. Edit the topics, never the generated files.
- `bun run docs:dev` serves the docs site, and `bun run release:check` packs the packages and builds a project from the tarballs.
- Decisions are recorded in `adrs/` (one file per decision, numbered). Specs, when present, are in `specs/`, which is kept out of git.
